newsitem.title: GERMANY: George-EMU criteria being pushed ahead by politics.
newsitem.headline: George-EMU criteria being pushed ahead by politics.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Tuesday that he was seeing some signs that the economic criteria for European monetary were being "pushed ahead" by political enthusiasm.
He also said that the real dangers for the euro lay in the potential for divergences in the domestic policy needs among the various participating nations of the single currency.

"Sustainable convergence from the outset is a precondition, if you do not have sustainable convergence I think it's an adventure," George said during a panel discussion during the Global 24 conference here.
"The purpose of convergence criteria is to ensure that there are not unacceptable divergences between the domestic policy needs of the different parts of the euro area," George said.

He also said, "The real dangers in the euro area lie in the potential for divergences between different member states...and there I think we have to emphasise the economics and not let the economics be overwritten by the politics.
"I'm afraid that I do see some signs that the economic criteria are being pushed ahead by the political enthusiam for which there is absolutely no mistaking the degree of political commitment."
